7.solution: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so it stays constant in an isothermal process.

Sodium citrate buffers are used in medicines: (C) - (II). The \(\mathrm{NH_4Cl/NH_4OH}\) buffer is used in qualitative analysis of basic radicals (group III): (D) - (III).

12.solution: Hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium salts (bicarbonates, chlorides and sulphates), that is \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ions.

13.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
13.solution: Ionisation enthalpy falls down a group as the atoms grow. The first members, Li in group 1 and Be in group 2, have the highest values.

14.solution: \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) dissolves in acids (\(\mathrm{Al_2O_3 + 6HCl \rightarrow 2AlCl_3 + 3H_2O}\)) and in alkalis (forming aluminates), so it is amphoteric.

15.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
15.solution: Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the phenoxide ion and raise acidity; electron-donating groups lower it. \(\mathrm{-NO_2}\) withdraws most strongly, \(\mathrm{-Cl}\) withdraws inductively, \(\mathrm{-CH_3}\) donates weakly and \(\mathrm{-OCH_3}\) donates by resonance. Order: III \(>\) I \(>\) II \(>\) IV.

16.subtopic: Electronic Effects, Hybridization, Intermediates and General Reactions
16.solution: Each alkyl group stabilises a carbocation by its +I effect and hyperconjugation. The tertiary cation \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\), with three methyl groups, is the most stable.

17.solution: Heating sodium benzoate with soda lime removes \(\mathrm{CO_2}\): \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COONa + NaOH \rightarrow C_6H_6 + Na_2CO_3}\). The product is benzene.

18.solution: An fcc cell has 4 Y atoms and 8 tetrahedral voids. One third of the voids gives \(\dfrac{8}{3}\) X atoms. \(X : Y = \dfrac{8}{3} : 4 = 2 : 3\), so the formula is \(X_2Y_3\).

Void volume \(= 3.793 \times 10^{-23} \times (1 - 0.5236) = 1.807 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).

20.solution: A Frenkel defect needs a small cation that can move into an interstitial site, and a large difference in ion sizes. ZnS has this; NaCl, KCl and KBr show Schottky defects.

24.solution: Oxidation takes place at the anode, so the anode reaction releases electrons. Only (C), \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + e^-}\), is an oxidation; the others are reductions.

25.solution: Reduction always occurs at the cathode. In a galvanic cell the cathode is the positive electrode, and electrodes must conduct.

27.solution: 32 minutes is two half-lives, so \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of the reactant remains and \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) has reacted.

29.solution: The unit of k is \((\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}})^{1-n}\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). A unit of \(\mathrm{s^{-1}}\) alone means \(n = 1\): a first order reaction.

30.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
30.solution: Butter is water dispersed in fat (water-in-oil). Milk and vanishing cream are oil-in-water emulsions.

31.subtopic: Group 16 Chalcogens, Oxygen, Sulphur and Ozone
31.solution: In ozone the two O-O bonds are equivalent by resonance, each about \(128\) pm, between an O-O single bond (148 pm) and an O=O double bond (121 pm).

32.solution: Unpaired electrons: \(\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}\) \(3d^1\) (1), \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) \(3d^3\) (3), \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\) \(3d^5\) (5), \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) \(3d^5\) (5), \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) \(3d^0\) (0). \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\) both have 5, so the same \(\mu = \sqrt{35}\) BM.

33.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
33.solution: Colour comes from d-d transitions, which need a partly filled d subshell. \(\mathrm{V^{3+}}\) is \(3d^2\). \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}\) are \(3d^0\) and \(\mathrm{Cu^+}\) is \(3d^{10}\), so they are colourless.

34.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
34.solution: \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\) is \(3d^4\). Cyanide is a strong-field ligand, so the four electrons pair up in three 3d orbitals, leaving two 3d orbitals free. With 4s and 4p these give \(d^2sp^3\) (inner orbital) hybridisation, an octahedral complex.

35.solution: In the Sandmeyer reaction a diazonium salt is treated with CuCl/HCl (or CuBr/HBr), replacing \(\mathrm{-N_2^+}\) by a halogen to give an aryl halide. (A) is Finkelstein, (C) Swarts and (D) Clemmensen.

38.solution: Acid-catalysed hydration of an alkene goes through a carbocation, so the alcohol forms most easily where the most stable cation can form: \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\).

39.solution: The iodoform test needs a \(\mathrm{CH_3CO-}\) group or a \(\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}\) group. Pentan-3-one, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3}\), has neither; the other three do.

40.solution: Ethyl methyl ketone and 3-methylbutan-2-one have \(\mathrm{CH_3CO-}\), and isopropyl alcohol has \(\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}\). Isobutyl alcohol, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH}\), is a primary alcohol without either group, so it cannot form iodoform.

41.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
41.solution: Electron-releasing alkyl groups destabilise the carboxylate ion and weaken the acid; chlorine strengthens it. The isopropyl group releases most electron density, so \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCOOH}\) is the weakest acid.

42.solution: Gabriel synthesis needs the phthalimide anion to displace a halide by \(\mathrm{S_N2}\). Aryl halides do not undergo this substitution, so aromatic primary amines such as aniline cannot be made this way.

43.solution: Isopropylamine is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHNH_2}\): nitrogen carries one alkyl group and two hydrogens, so it is a primary amine (whatever the carbon it is attached to).

44.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
44.solution: A pairs with T and G with C, and the strands run antiparallel. Opposite 5'-GACGTAC-3' the complementary strand reads 3'-CTGCATG-5'.

45.solution: Starch (amylose and amylopectin) is a polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose joined by \(\alpha\)-glycosidic links. Cellulose is the polymer of \(\beta\)-D-glucose.

47.solution: Polythene forms by addition of ethene molecules across their double bonds. Nylon 6, Dacron and Nylon 6,6 are condensation (step-growth) polymers.

48.solution: Teflon is made by addition (chain-growth) polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene. The nylons and terylene are step-growth polymers.

49.solution: Formalin, a \(40\%\) aqueous solution of formaldehyde, is best known for preserving biological and anatomical specimens.

51.subtopic: Roots — Nature, Vieta's Relations, and Conditions
51.solution:
Take the polynomials monic: \(p(x) = (x - 1)(x - \alpha)\) and \(q(x) = (x - 1)(x - \beta)\). Then \(r(x) = 2x^2 - (2 + \alpha + \beta)x + (\alpha + \beta)\).

Its roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\): sum \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{2 + \alpha + \beta}{2}\) gives \(\alpha + \beta = 2\), and product \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2} = 1\). So \(\alpha = \beta = 1\).

Then \(p = q = (x - 1)^2\), so \(\sqrt{p(x)} - \sqrt{q(x)} = 0\) and the limit is \(0\).

\(\sin(x + \alpha)\sin(x - \alpha) = \sin^2 x - \sin^2\alpha\), and \(\sin 3\alpha = 3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^3\alpha\).

Dividing by \(4\sin\alpha \neq 0\): \(\dfrac{3}{4} - \sin^2\alpha = \sin^2 x - \sin^2\alpha\), so \(\sin^2 x = \dfrac{3}{4} = \sin^2\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(x = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3}\).

54.solution:
Let \(u = \theta - \alpha\) and \(X = \alpha - \beta\), so \(\theta - \beta = u + X\) and \(b = \sin(u + X) = \sin u\cos X + a\sin X\).

Then \(b - a\sin X = \sin u\cos X\). Squaring: \(b^2 - 2ab\sin X + a^2\sin^2 X = (1 - a^2)\cos^2 X\), which rearranges to \(\cos^2 X + 2ab\sin X = a^2 + b^2\).

The expression is \(a^2 + b^2 + \cos^2(\theta - \alpha) = a^2 + b^2 + a^2 = 2a^2 + b^2\).

56.solution:
Let the line meet the axes at \(A(a, 0)\) and \(B(0, b)\). The point dividing AB in the ratio \(4 : 3\) is \(\left(\dfrac{3a}{7}, \dfrac{4b}{7}\right) = (-5, 3)\), so \(a = -\dfrac{35}{3}\) and \(b = \dfrac{21}{4}\).

\(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\): \(-\dfrac{3x}{35} + \dfrac{4y}{21} = 1\). Multiplying by 105: \(-9x + 20y = 105\), that is \(9x - 20y + 105 = 0\).

62.subtopic: Finding Truth Values of Component Statements
62.solution:
The implication is false only when the antecedent is T and \(p \wedge q\) is F. Then \(\sim r\) is T (r is F), \(q \to r\) is T (q is F), and \(p \vee q\) is T (p is T).

With \(p = \mathrm{T}\), \(q = \mathrm{F}\): \(p \to q\) is F and \(q \to p\) is T.

The r-th term is \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1 + (x + r - 1)(x + r)} = \tan^{-1}(x + r) - \tan^{-1}(x + r - 1)\), so the sum telescopes: \(y = \tan^{-1}(x + n) - \tan^{-1}x\).

\(y' = \dfrac{1}{1 + (x + n)^2} - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\), and \(y'(0) = \dfrac{1}{1 + n^2} - 1 = -\dfrac{n^2}{n^2 + 1}\).

Let \(u = \sqrt{y + x}\), \(w = \sqrt{y - x}\). Then \(u + w = c\) and \(u^2 - w^2 = 2x\), so \(u - w = \dfrac{2x}{c}\). Hence \(y = \dfrac{u^2 + w^2}{2} = \dfrac{c^2}{4} + \dfrac{x^2}{c^2}\) and \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x}{c^2}\).

With \(f = \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{c^2}{4x} + \dfrac{x}{c^2}\): \(f^2 - 1 = \left(\dfrac{c^2}{4x} - \dfrac{x}{c^2}\right)^2\), so \(f - \sqrt{f^2 - 1} = \dfrac{2x}{c^2} = \dfrac{dy}{dx}\). So \(f(x) = \dfrac{y}{x}\).

104.solution:
With air friction negligible, gravity gives both balls the same acceleration g, so they land together.

One might expect eddy currents in the metal ball from the earth's magnetic field to slow it. But the earth's field is uniform over the ball, and a conductor moving in a straight line through a uniform field has no changing flux through any loop inside it: the motional emf only separates a little charge and drives no circulating current. So there is no retarding force, and both reach the surface simultaneously.
